acceptanceGrade: REJECT-ON-ONE-OMISSION. Everything the artifact says is true and well-sourced, including a hard empirical audit and a hard negative claim I tested directly. What fails is completeness against the artifact's own stated scope: one of the four recorded D-012 deferrals is missing.

shouldFix.title: One of the four recorded D-012 deferrals — the support/vulnerability policy side routed to DR-116 — is absent from the join
shouldFix.finding: The artifact's purpose undertakes to split, among other things, 'the D-012 deferred items'. D-012's adopted bytes state the routing in a single clause: 'namespace depth beyond the mounted-root model AND third-party transfer/dispute policy are both EXPLICITLY DEFERRED to the DR-117 successor process (owned by DR-010), with DR-116 carrying the support/vulnerability policy side'. D-130's recorded corpus — which this join pins — lists four explicitlyDeferred items: the two DR-117 items, the DR-116 support/vulnerability side, and the DR-114 migration-doctor fixture. The join carries three of the four. OBL-DEFERRED-DR117 covers the two DR-117 items and OBL-MIGRATION-DOCTOR covers the DR-114 ride; nothing covers DR-116. The strings DR-116, support and vulnerab each occur zero times in the artifact.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: The join presents its six obligations as a complete partition of DR-104's obligations, and a later act will read it as the inventory of what is deferred and where. Three-quarters of a recorded four-item deferral list is not that inventory. The omission is also selective rather than principled: the missing item sits in the same D-012 sentence as the two the artifact does carry, and in the same corpus field.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocker: Nothing false is asserted and the eligibility conclusion is unaffected. The missing item is a routing to another row, so it belongs in deferredOrRidesElsewhere rather than in leftover-design; its absence cannot understate leftover or overstate D-056 standing, which is what a blocker here would require.
shouldFix.repair: Add an obligation in the shape of OBL-MIGRATION-DOCTOR — for example OBL-DEFERRED-DR116, leftoverDesign false, existingGate 'none on DR-104. Deferred by D-012 to DR-116', rideStanding deferred-to-DR-116 — citing D-012's routing clause and D-130's explicitlyDeferred item, and add it to summary.deferredOrRidesElsewhere. Add a matching refusal that the join does not retarget DR-116.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Thirteen attacks run, one landed, and the repair is additive. Custody holds: subject 48d418b6 at 0444 unmoved with dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left 23fe6d9, file 08 at 3a9442d1 equal to the subject's own pin, governing tree clean. Almost everything here is right and I verified the two hardest claims myself. The fixture audit replicates exactly — eleven classes, eleven primaries, six also-bytes, seventeen files, zero mismatches, every class carrying a primary. The load-bearing negative claim also holds: I scanned all thirty live gate claims, and no gate owns identity-namespace negative-test execution, so classifying that remainder as leftover rather than forcing a ride onto G15 is correct rather than merely cautious. The row token is DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED as the artifact says, the DR-104 row does place negative-test evidence at qualification, D-131 did record v4 as the leftover-integration T2-02 candidate, and D-130's recorded corpus does state twice that the migration doctor rides DR-114 and is not a twelfth class — that one is in the artifact, not in D-130's COORD summary, which is the same lesson D-161 taught. The objection is a coverage gap. The artifact's own purpose undertakes to split the D-012 deferred items, and both D-012 and the pinned D-130 corpus record four of them: namespace depth and third-party transfer to the DR-117 successor, the support/vulnerability policy side to DR-116, and the migration-doctor fixture to DR-114. The join carries three. DR-116, support and vulnerab occur zero times in it, and the missing item sits in the same D-012 sentence and the same corpus field as items the artifact does carry. I graded it SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker because it is a routing to another row, so its absence cannot understate leftover-design or overstate D-056 standing — unlike the OD-2 omission Codex charged as a blocker at DR-103, which was an undecided decision. I record that comparison because Codex may weigh it the other way. The finding came from running exactly the check I failed to run on that DR-103 join: enumerating the pinned contract's own inventory before reading the subject's account of it.
